questions.prompt: What does the ID T1055.012 represent?
options: A sub-technique -- Process Hollowing, one specific way of achieving Process Injection
A tactic within the Execution phase
questions.explanation: The dot notation is a hierarchy, not a version. A sub-technique is a narrower variant of its parent technique.

questions.prompt: Which ATT&CK section most directly identifies instrumentation gaps?
options: Data Sources, which list what telemetry can detect the technique
questions.explanation: Data Sources answer 'what would I need to be logging to see this', converting an ATT&CK reference into a concrete telemetry requirement -- the most useful and least-read section.

questions.prompt: Why can a single technique appear under multiple tactics?
options: It is a data-quality error in the framework
Tactics describe the adversary's goal, and one action can serve several -- Process Injection achieves both Defense Evasion and Privilege Escalation
Techniques are randomly assigned to tactics
Only deprecated techniques appear more than once
questions.explanation: Because tactics represent goals rather than sequential stages, the same technique legitimately serves more than one, which is why ATT&CK is not a linear kill chain.

questions.prompt: Why is 'we cover 80% of ATT&CK' close to meaningless?
options: ATT&CK does not publish a technique count
Techniques are not equally weighted or equally relevant to any environment, and covering a technique does not mean covering every procedure implementing it
Coverage can only be measured by MITRE directly
80% is below the minimum acceptable threshold
questions.explanation: ATT&CK is a shared vocabulary and coverage-reasoning tool, not a maturity score. Percentage coverage flattens away everything that makes the framework useful.
